function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can follow (or copy into a script) to finish the task.  
I’ll also give you the exact files you need to create/modify so you can paste them straight into the repo.

> ⚠️ **Important** – I don’t have direct access to your machine or the repo, so I can’t actually run `git clone`, `git add`, `git commit` or `git push`.  
> You’ll need to execute those commands yourself (or run this from a CI job that has the proper SSH key / PAT).

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# Make sure you have an SSH key added to your GitHub account
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

If you prefer HTTPS:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & create/update files

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Assuming the repo is a simple Express/Node app that listens on port **3000** (the most common default), here’s a minimal Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Copy only the files needed for installing dependencies
COPY package*.json ./

RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source
COPY . .

# Build step (if you have a build script)
# RUN npm run build

EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

*If the entry point is different (`server.js`, `index.js`, etc.), change the `CMD` accordingly.*

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Create a file called `k8s/deployment.yaml` (you can keep it under a `k8s/` folder or at the repo root):

```yaml
# k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry/tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80          # Service port
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
  type: ClusterIP
```

> **Tip:** If you want external access, change `type: ClusterIP` to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer`.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml`:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write   # Needed to push to GHCR

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          file: ./Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **Prerequisites**  
> *Make sure the repo has the `GHCR` scope enabled for the `GITHUB_TOKEN`.*  
> If you’re using a personal access token instead, store it as a secret named `GHCR_PAT` and replace `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` with `${{ secrets.GHCR_PAT }}`.

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new/updated files to git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
```

If you created the `k8s/` folder, add it too:

```bash
git add k8s/
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

Once pushed, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically trigger on the next push to `main` and build/push the Docker image to `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`.

---

### Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Dockerfile (under repo root) |
| ✅ | Kubernetes YAML (`k8s/deployment.yaml`) |
| ✅ | GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/docker-build.yml`) |
| ✅ | `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` |

Feel free to tweak the image names, tags, replica counts, or service types to match your environment. Once you’ve pushed, you can deploy the manifests with:

```bash
kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml
```

Happy deploying!
